title: The Mirage of Calibrated Confidence: Verbalized Confidence in Vision-Language Models

summary.claim: A VLM's verbalized confidence is largely independent of its reasoning: it can revise its reasoning, end up wrong, and still report high confidence. Calibration training can make this worse, and ECE and AUROC do not show it.
summary.condition: TGS-Bench with good/bad reasoning trajectory pairs over 10 benchmarks; TGS-self and TGS-pair metrics.
summary.gap: (Authors) Results are limited to the VLMs and calibration methods tested. (Inferred) Whether text LLMs or internal-representation confidence show the same gap is open.
